files.code: FIT/CHECK/HELDOUT public split, admission and hashed source labels

observed_public_contract.initial_state: Two public 4-bit state values per entity
observed_public_contract.target_source: Public selected source and destination entity names; causal role selection is visible as a time-ordered action context
observed_public_contract.outcome: Public four-bit observed target outcome; state update of target pair is derivable from history
observed_public_contract.previous_CHECK: 8 eight-event veto trajectories; do not train
observed_public_contract.previous_heldout: 8 eight-event terminal diagnostic trajectories; do not select model

interpretation.positive: Time-resolved public entity names, directed source/target slots, pre-event entity states, event covariates and observed outcomes provide a meaningful supervised basis for learning entity-binding and causal transition prediction.
interpretation.limiting: The parser and frozen split alone do not establish independently controlled interventions that hold confounding constant or identify arbitrary do-counterfactuals. An event's directed target/source labels are not a proof of randomized intervention or unique causal direction.
interpretation.identifiability: LCRM01-A analytic equivalence proof still applies to observation-only subclasses. Any original causal intervention claim must show public authentic action assignment, temporal consistency and a discriminating contrast; otherwise abstain.
interpretation.source_reuse: This is a READ of historical public-interface source code, not case generation, replay, fitting, recovered heldout information or reuse of consumed results as new first-use.

next_eligible_gate: LCRM01-B2: independent audit of publicly authenticated intervention assignments and source-neutral causal discrimination; then implement candidate and equally trained recurrent/relational + symbolic controls. Before prospective first-use, freeze all architectures, labels, budgets and independent source birth. Halt if the public source cannot discriminate causal mechanisms.
